Ángeles — Madrid, Spain

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 131 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Reviewed — no findings area reviewed, nothing documented — not a safety rating

In detail

Searches for the official 'Angeles' barrio specifically (distinct from the much more heavily covered 'San Cristobal de los Angeles', which is San Cristobal barrio's older/colloquial full name) returned no coverage genuinely distinct from San Cristobal's own narcopiso and robbery reporting. No particular safety concern found in the source review specific to this exact barrio, and San Cristobal's own findings are not attributed here to avoid conflating the two. Sources checked: Google search for barrio 'Angeles' Villaverde: results returned were about San Cristobal de los Angeles (a different official barrio), not Angeles itself.

This area was reviewed as part of a structured local-source assessment — the same area-level review applied to every neighbourhood in Madrid, drawing on local and national news, municipal and police-published material and official surveys where they exist. The review reached nothing traveller-relevant for this area, so it carries no rating. That is deliberate: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe, and Wandroz does not convert one into the other.

Frequently asked questions

Is Ángeles safe?

Ángeles was reviewed at area level and no traveller-relevant safety concern was documented for it in the sources checked. Wandroz records that as no findings, not as a safety rating: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Why does Ángeles have no rating?

Because the review found nothing to rate it on. Areas with documented, sourced signals get a level; areas without them are shown as reviewed with no findings, so you can tell the difference between an area that was checked and came back clear of documented issues and one that was never looked at. Both are treated as inconclusive here rather than as reassurance.

Is Ángeles a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it, and nothing documented argues for it either. For a stay, weigh it against the rated areas on the Madrid map and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
